skill.name: claude-reflect
skill.description: Self-learning system that captures corrections during sessions and reminds users to run /reflect to update CLAUDE.md. Use when discussing learnings, corrections, or when the user mentions remembering something for future sessions.
skill.summary: Captures your corrections during Claude Code sessions and applies them to CLAUDE.md memory after review.
skill.author: BayramAnnakov

security_audit.summary: claude-reflect is a documentation-only Claude Code plugin corpus (8 Markdown/text files, no executable scripts in scope). All 91 static findings were adjudicated as false positives: the `~/.claude/*` references are the plugin's own documented memory-hierarchy and queue storage, the two CRITICAL `rm -rf` hits are user-facing cache-clearing instructions scoped to a specific named plugin-cache subdirectory in the README troubleshooting section, the 'backtick execution' hits are Markdown inline-code/code-fence syntax, and the hardcoded URLs point to the project's own public repository. No prompt-injection, data-exfiltration, or business-logic-abuse intent was found.

remediation.issue: Troubleshooting docs instruct users to run `rm -rf` on `~/.claude/plugins/...` cache paths, which security scanners flag as high-risk.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer targeted removals or a documented helper command over `rm -rf` on home-directory paths, and add an inline note warning users to verify the exact path before running.

content.user_title: Capture corrections and update your CLAUDE.md memory
content.value_statement: Claude Code forgets your corrections between sessions, so you repeat the same guidance again and again. claude-reflect captures those corrections automatically and lets you review and apply them to your CLAUDE.md memory files with one command.
actual_capabilities: Detects correction patterns in your prompts, such as 'no, use X' or 'actually', using a hooks-based capture stage.
Queues detected learnings to a local JSON file for later review.
Provides a /reflect command that reviews queued learnings with human approval before writing.
Routes approved learnings to the correct memory target, including global, project, and rule files.
Scans past session files for missed corrections with /reflect --scan-history.
Suggests reusable skill candidates from repeating patterns with /reflect-skills.
limitations: It writes only to Markdown memory files; it does not change your code or run your tools.
Correction detection depends on recognizable phrasing and may miss subtle guidance.
The semantic analysis step requires the Claude CLI to be available.
It is designed for Claude Code and its CLAUDE.md hierarchy, not general note-taking.

use_cases.title: Stop repeating the same corrections
use_cases.description: A developer who keeps telling Claude Code the same project conventions can capture those corrections once and apply them to the project CLAUDE.md file.

use_cases.title: Keep team conventions in sync
use_cases.description: A team lead can review queued learnings before they are written, so shared CLAUDE.md files stay accurate and reviewed.

use_cases.title: Recover missed learnings from past work
use_cases.description: A user returning to a project can scan past sessions to find corrections that were never saved and add them to memory.

prompt_templates.title: Review queued learnings
prompt_templates.prompt: Run /reflect and show me the learnings that are queued before applying any of them.

prompt_templates.title: Preview changes safely
prompt_templates.prompt: Run /reflect --dry-run so I can see what would change in my CLAUDE.md files without writing anything.

prompt_templates.title: Scan history for missed learnings
prompt_templates.prompt: Run /reflect --scan-history and list corrections from past sessions that were never saved.

prompt_templates.title: Discover reusable skills
prompt_templates.prompt: Run /reflect-skills over the last 30 days and propose skill candidates from repeating patterns, but do not create any files yet.

output_examples.input: no, use gpt-5.1 not gpt-5 for reasoning tasks
output_examples.output: The correction is captured to the local queue. On the next /reflect run, it is offered as the learning 'Use gpt-5.1 for reasoning tasks' with a suggested global scope, and you approve before it is written.
One learning is found in the queue. You are shown the learning text, its suggested memory target, and a yes or no prompt to apply it.

best_practices: Review learnings with /reflect --dry-run before applying them so you can see the exact changes.
Run /reflect at natural stopping points, such as after finishing a feature or before context compaction.
Choose the narrowest memory target that fits, using project files for project rules and global files only for broad patterns.
anti_patterns: Do not apply every queued learning without reading it, because low-value corrections can clutter your memory files.
Do not store secrets, tokens, or personal data in captured learnings, since memory files persist across sessions.
Do not rely on capture alone to remember important rules; run /reflect so learnings are actually written.

faq.question: What does claude-reflect do?
faq.answer: It captures your corrections during a session and lets you review and apply them to your CLAUDE.md memory files with the /reflect command.

faq.question: Does it change my files without asking?
faq.answer: No. Capture is automatic, but writing to memory files happens only after you review and approve the learnings.

faq.question: Where are learnings stored before I apply them?
faq.answer: Detected learnings are queued in a local JSON file under your Claude Code home directory until you process them.

faq.question: Which memory files can it write to?
faq.answer: It can target global, project, local, rule, and auto-memory files in the standard CLAUDE.md hierarchy, based on the scope you approve.

faq.question: Can it find corrections I already missed?
faq.answer: Yes. The /reflect --scan-history command scans past session files for corrections that were never saved.

faq.question: What does it require to run?
faq.answer: It is a Claude Code plugin and needs Python 3.6 or later; the semantic analysis step also uses the Claude CLI when available.
